questions.question: When riding in a group, what is the best way to stay close together while keeping safe distance between riders?

options.text: In pairs.
In a staggered formation.
In a single-file line.
In a passing formation.

questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close while keeping safe distance between them. Use single-file when riding through curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway. Never ride side-by-side with another rider.

questions.question: Alcohol does not need to be digested like food. What does this mean?

options.text: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the rider right away.
The alcohol never leaves the body.
It takes a long time to feel the effects of alcohol.
Your body gets rid of alcohol very quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol reaches the brain within minutes and starts to affect the rider right away.
questions.explanation: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, it enters the bloodstream quickly and reaches the brain within minutes. The body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What happens when alcohol and drugs are used together?

options.text: The effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
The effects are less dangerous than when either is used alone.
The effects are usually mild.
The effects often cancel each other out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The effects are stronger than when either is used alone.
questions.explanation: Many drugs, including prescription and over-the-counter medicines, can make it unsafe to ride. Some medicines become even more dangerous when mixed with alcohol.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's stopping power comes from the front brake?

options.text: About one-quarter
About one-half
About three-quarters
All the stopping power

questions.explanation: The front brake is stronger than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: What is a good way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up may only make things more dangerous by making them follow you at a higher speed.

questions.question: What is true about more than half of all motorcycle crashes?

options.text: They happen at speeds greater than 35 mph.
They happen at night.
They are caused by worn tires.
They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They involve riders with less than six months of experience on that motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Be extra careful when riding a new or unfamiliar motorcycle. Most crashes happen to riders who have had the motorcycle for less than six months.

questions.question: In Illinois, which of these is allowed on a motorcycle?

options.text: A modified muffler that makes it louder.
Handlebars higher than the rider's head when seated.
A blue license plate light.
A seat designed to carry two people.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat designed to carry two people.
questions.explanation: In Illinois, all motorcycles must have a white license plate light. Making mufflers louder is not allowed. Handlebars must not be higher than the rider's head when seated normally. Passengers can only ride if the motorcycle and seat are designed for two people.

questions.question: If one of your tires goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Roll on the throttle.
Hold the handlebars loosely.
Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
Go faster to exit the road quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat.
questions.explanation: If one tire goes flat, ease off the throttle and keep going straight as you slow down. If you must brake, gently apply the brake on the tire that is not flat, if you are sure which one it is.

questions.question: When can motorcycles pass on the right?

options.text: If there is at least eight feet of clear road.
By riding on the shoulder.
By riding on the grass, if it is level.

questions.correctAnswerText: If there is at least eight feet of clear road.
questions.explanation: Motorcyclists can pass on the right only if there is at least eight feet of clear pavement to the right of the vehicle being passed. Never leave the road to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: In Illinois, at what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is a person considered intoxicated?

options.text: 0.02 percent
0.04 percent
0.08 percent
0.1 percent

questions.explanation: In Illinois, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means a person is legally intoxicated. It is illegal and dangerous for an intoxicated person to operate a motorcycle or any vehicle.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, what should you do?

options.text: Kick the dog away.
Stop and let the dog lose interest.
Swerve around the dog.
Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as you approach the dog, then speed up and leave it behind.
questions.explanation: Dogs often chase motorcycles. If a dog is chasing you, slow down and approach it carefully. Then speed up and drive away from it.

questions.question: When passing parked cars on your right and there is no oncoming traffic, where should you ride?

options.text: Stay toward the right side of your lane.
Stay toward the left side of your lane.
Look to your left frequently.
Use your rearview mirrors more than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay toward the left side of your lane.
questions.explanation: When passing parked cars, stay on the side of your lane away from the cars. This protects you from car doors opening or people stepping out. This distance gives you more time to react to dangers.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in the rearview mirror of the car ahead?

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Ride in the left portion of the lane.
Ride in the right portion of the lane.
Ride in a weaving pattern.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of the lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind the car ahead. This puts you directly in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: Illinois law requires that motorcycle headlights be:

options.text: Used at all times.
Used only between dusk and sunrise.
Used only when there is no bright sunlight.
Turned off when stopped in traffic.

questions.explanation: Illinois law requires you to use your motorcycle headlight at all times while riding. All motorcycles sold in the United States since 1978 have headlights that turn on automatically when the engine runs.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours passed from the number of drinks consumed. Eight drinks minus four hours equals four drinks remaining in the body.
